title: Large graphs after object boxes: 300-node cap reached by ordinary pandas code
description: From PR #38 review: a 98-line pandas-heavy program goes from 265 nodes (main before svl-skw) to 459 (141 instances, 80 calls, 63 exprs, 16 stores) and is truncated at ~line 65; the rest silently vanishes. Needs: (1) a clear visible 'diagram truncated at line N — showing the first 300 boxes' notice (and in the event list); (2) a way to keep big programs usable: e.g. raise the cap with the layout tiers (measure), and/or fold unnamed intermediate objects (no variable binding, single consumer, e.g. df['sqft'].isna()) into the wire between producer and consumer with an expand affordance. Owner wanted every object explicit, so folding must be opt-out/expandable and documented; ask the owner before making folding the default.
acceptance_criteria: The 98-line repro (rv38/progs in the coordinator scratchpad, or an equivalent new fixture) renders completely or shows a clear truncation notice; layout stays within budget; no-false-wires checks pass.
notes: Owner decisions (2026-11-19), all three: (1) FOLLOW THE CURRENT STEP: keep everything, but the diagram view auto-zooms to a readable scale (e.g. >= 80%) and pans to the current step's boxes (current node + its inputs/outputs + owning instance) as the student steps; 'Fit' still shows the whole graph; user pan/zoom suspends following until the next step or a 'Follow' toggle. (2) FOLD UNNAMED TEMPORARIES: objects never bound to a variable and consumed exactly once (e.g. df['sqft'].isna(), X_train[['neighbourhood']]) fold into the wire between producer and consumer as a small chip (type + shape), expandable on click to the full box; named objects always get boxes. Must not create false wires (the folded wire still runs producer -> consumer for that token only). (3) RAISE THE CAP above 300 (measure with the layout tiers; e.g. 600–800) and show a visible 'truncated at line N' notice if a cap is still hit. Repro: coordinator scratchpad rv38/progs (98-line pandas program).
close_reason: Merged PR #42 after review (no false wires; 10 adversarial programs). Follow the current step (follow.ts: focus = current node + wired neighbours + owning instance, 80–100% zoom, manual pan/zoom suspends until the student steps; not reset by streamed steps; Follow toggle persisted; reduced motion). Fold unnamed temporaries (buildGraph fold default true: never bound/mutated/ctor-made, output once, used once later by a non-expr event) into chip wires, expandable per chip, 'All objects' toggle. Cap raised to 600 with 'Showing the first N boxes (up to line L)' notice. New fixture large_pandas.py (364 boxes folded, ~0.5 s layout). Dense 600-box slow test budget 15 s.

title: Vertical timeline as a rail in the code gutter, tied to source lines
description:
Owner decision (2026-11-18): the timeline should be vertical and obviously tied to the lines of code. Loops repeat lines, so the timeline becomes a rail in the editor gutter (between line numbers and code):
- Each executed line gets one marker per recorded event on that line, in time order (● ran, ◉ current, ○ not yet reached). A line with several calls (df = pd.read_csv(...).dropna()) shows one dot per event.
- Loop lines show one dot per iteration; beyond ~8 executions collapse to a compact '×n' chip with a mini scrubber / 'k of n' when current.
- The playhead (▶ + the existing strong line highlight from svl-a6x) sits on the current line; stepping through a loop visibly jumps back up.
- Interaction: click a dot → that step; ↑/↓ (or j/k) and Home/End step through time when the rail or diagram has focus; the slider and event list remain available (move the horizontal slider into a compact control under the diagram, or replace it — keep a screen-reader-friendly event list as today).
- Uses existing pure helpers (stepOfEvent, stateAt, eventLabel; steps.ts). Keep pure logic (line → events/steps mapping, collapse rule, keyboard stepping) in plain functions with unit tests.
- Sites are only valid while the doc equals runSource: after an edit the rail clears (same rule as highlights).
- Light/dark, keyboard path, not colour-only (shapes/fill differ), works at 768px.
Update SPEC 'Timeline' and CONTRACTS §10 as needed.
acceptance_criteria: Starter example and edge_loop in the browser: dots on executed lines, loop body lines show per-iteration dots or ×n, current dot and line obvious, clicking a dot / ↑↓ steps and the diagram follows; after editing the code the rail clears; light/dark + 768px screenshots; unit tests for mapping/collapse/keyboard.
close_reason: Merged PR #36 (coordinator-read + screenshot check). Gutter rail: one dot per event per line (filled ran, ring current, hollow not yet), >8 executions collapse to ×n chip showing 'k of n' when current; click dot/chip steps; gutter focusable (role=slider) with Down/j later, Up/k earlier, Home/End; rail clears after an edit. Slider kept as compact control under the diagram (diagram keeps Up/Down for pan, steps with Left/Right, j/k). SPEC Timeline + CONTRACTS §10 item 24.

title: Every object is a blue box: DataFrames, Series, arrays and other reference values become instance boxes
description:
Owner decision (2026-11-18): not all objects are explicitly displayed today — data (DataFrame, Series, ndarray, …) travels as labelled wires and only machines (estimators, student classes) get blue instance boxes. The owner wants every object as its own blue box, like models. Design (coordinator defaults, adjust in SPEC if needed):
- Every reference value (ValueTable classify == reference: DataFrame, Series, ndarray, sparse, list/dict/tuple, models, student objects) gets an instance box, one per object (object number); in-place mutation = a new version of the same box (attribute rows update). Scalars and labels stay as before (port text / wire labels / const ports).
- A function that returns an object (pd.read_csv, train_test_split's four outputs, np.mean returning an array) has an out-port wired to the new object's box border; consumers take wires from the box border (like machines today). Wire labels drop the type/shape (the box shows it) and keep the variable name.
- Methods called on an object go inside its box, one box per method name (same rule as svl-2gm): df.dropna() is a dropna box inside the df box whose output wire creates the df′ box (rebinding prime as today).
- Data boxes show a few attributes from the summary: shape, dtype or dtypes/columns (truncated), not the full value. Click shows the preview (svl-bwv.5 inspect).
- Expression nodes stay (dashed) but their result object is a box: y = df['price'] → expr node from df box → y box.
- No false wires: one box per object identity (the recorder's tokens), never merge two objects; a missing wire is still acceptable.
- Graph size: more nodes; keep the 300-node cap and layout tiers working; measure golden/heavy/notebook.
Build on svl-2gm's instance/method-slot model (generalise 'machine' to 'object' in graph.ts/timeline.ts), update SPEC (machine table, wires, Q list) and CONTRACTS §8, golden slide assertions (golden_split: read_csv → df box; dropna inside df box → df′ box; split outputs four boxes), regenerate fixtures/graphs. Renderer/layout changes needed for data boxes go to svl-0qe unless trivial.
acceptance_criteria: golden_split/onehot/linreg graphs show every DataFrame/Series/array as its own instance box with the right wires; methods on data inside their object's box; no-false-wires check over all fixtures passes; layout under budget on fixtures (heavy, notebook); SPEC + CONTRACTS updated.
notes: From PR #34 review: golden.test.ts no-false-wires check uses <= for instance consumers; ret === createdAt holds for all fixtures, tighten to === when widening isObject. Places to revisit when widening isObject: drawnInputs self-port rule, mutates -> instance versions instead of out:mut ports, timeline.ts ownerAttrs checks values[owner].machine.
close_reason: Merged PR #38 after review (no false wires). Every v-token is an instance box; methods on data inside it (no self port); in-place method mutation = new version; call returning its argument adds nothing; object ports typeLabel '', wires out of boxes nameLabel null; data rows shape + dtype/columns. Primes: new binding gets the prime (df, df′, df″, cap ‴); loop objects from one site share one box with the first name. No-false-wires check tightened (ret === i; no object token as source; no object in two boxes). ~1.8x nodes, layout time unchanged on fixtures.

title: Docs source: structured official documentation for any function, class or method, plus a versioned link
description:
Owner request (2026-11-18): every function, class and method in the UI can show its official documentation in a friendly way, plus a link to the full docs. Privacy rule: the page fetches nothing off-origin, so the content comes from the docstrings installed in Pyodide; the link is a plain <a target=_blank rel=noopener> the student clicks.
Build: python/machines/docs.py with docs(target) -> {qualname, kind, signature, summary, sections: {Parameters: [{name, type, desc}], Returns, Raises, See Also, Notes, Examples (code blocks)}, url|null, source: 'numpydoc'|'plain'|'none'}. target is either a value token/qualname resolved in the worker (event callee: module+name; method: owner class mro + method name; class). Parse numpydoc (sklearn/pandas/numpy/scipy/matplotlib) with a small stdlib parser (no new runtime deps), fall back to plain text. Student functions/classes: their own docstring, url null. Builtins: docs.python.org.
URL builder (pure, unit-tested, version-pinned from the running packages): sklearn https://scikit-learn.org/<major.minor>/modules/generated/<qualname>.html (methods: anchor #<qualname>.<method>); pandas https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/version/<ver>/reference/api/<qualname>.html; numpy https://numpy.org/doc/<major.minor>/reference/generated/<qualname>.html; scipy, matplotlib similarly; builtins https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/functions.html#<name>. Use the public qualname (e.g. sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression, not the private module path).
Worker: a new request/response message pair (ToWorker 'docs' {reqId, target}; FromWorker 'docs' {reqId, doc}) handled between runs and also during idle; RuntimeClient.docs(target): Promise<Doc>. Never during a run's critical path; cache results per target in the client. CONTRACTS §7 + a new docs section; SPEC: add a 'Documentation' section.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: numpydoc parser on LinearRegression, LinearRegression.fit, pandas.read_csv, numpy.mean, train_test_split, a student function, a builtin; URL builder exact strings for each library at the pinned versions (and resolves to the public path); worker round-trip test with the fake worker; no network in tests; transparency unaffected.
close_reason: Merged PR #35 (coordinator-read; additive). python/machines/docs.py: docs(module, name, source) -> Doc {qualname, kind, signature (self removed), summary, description, sections[] (entries/seealso/examples/text), url|null, source numpydoc|plain|none}; numpydoc parser tested on real sklearn/pandas/numpy/scipy/mpl docstrings (32 tests, also in Pyodide). Versioned URLs per library (public qualname via shortest re-exporting module; methods anchor on class page; builtins docs.python.org). Worker 'docs' request/response; RuntimeClient.docs(target) cached per target, in-flight shared, rejected on restart. Student targets need source (parsed with ast, never executed). Off-origin fetch exception not used (COEP would block); CSP unchanged. CONTRACTS §7, §12; SPEC 'Documentation'.

title: Graph: constructor call box creates the instance; one method box per method, present from instantiation
description: Owner decisions (2026-11-18): (1) a constructor call (LinearRegression(), OneHotEncoder(...)) is drawn as a function-call box with its args on ports, whose output wire creates the instance box (today the constructor merges into the instance and its args become the instance's param list). (2) Inside an instance, one method box per *method name* (not per call site): two enc.transform calls share one 'transform' box with ×2, wires switching per execution. (3) Method boxes exist from the moment the instance is created: they are visible (in a 'not called yet' state) from createdAt, and become active/called at their first execution; this must be expressible in StepState. Which methods: the ones the program calls on that instance in this run. (An expandable 'more methods' list comes from svl values/renderer beads.) Update SPEC.md (machine table, Q at line ~378 resolved: one box per method) and CONTRACTS §8 (GraphModel: ctor CallNode with createdBy edge to instance; method box key = (instance, method name); StepState: method slots visible-but-uncalled), graph.ts, timeline.ts, golden assertions (golden_onehot now one transform ×2; golden_linreg ctor box -> instance), regenerate fixtures/graphs. No false wires: a method box's per-execution wires come from that execution only.

title: Layout performance on dense graphs (300 nodes / ~600 edges takes ~29 s)
description: PR #16 review measured main's layout() on a dense 300-node, 593-edge graph (chain plus fan-in from 7 hubs, no instances) at ~29 s, and ~22 s with 10 instances. SPEC 'Layout' assumes ELK is fast enough for a few hundred nodes; svl-bwv.4 re-lays out while streaming. Investigate ELK options (e.g. crossingMinimization thoroughness, cycle breaking, layered.compaction, mergeEdges, separateConnectedComponents), hierarchyHandling INCLUDE_CHILDREN cost, and a size-based degradation (e.g. simpler options above N nodes/edges, or collapsing wires with many uses). Add a benchmark test with dense shapes.
acceptance_criteria: Dense 300-node/600-edge graph lays out in < 2 s in vitest (warm), with and without instances; determinism and existing geometric tests still pass; chosen options documented in CONTRACTS section 8.
close_reason: Merged PR #19 after review fixes. Size tiers by longEdgeLoad (an estimate): tier 0 (<=4000) unchanged options; tier 1 (<=15000) considerModelOrder NONE + thoroughness 1; tier 2 (no compound nodes only) adds crossingMinimization NONE + SEPARATE_CHILDREN. placeLabels grid-indexed, byte-identical to before. Dense 300/~600: 1.1 s without instances, 2.4 s with 10 instances (gap vs 2 s target). Exported tierFor(load) and LayoutOptions.minTier: bwv.4 must keep the tier sticky per run (max seen, reset on new run). Dense instance test + timing bounds run only in pnpm test:slow.

title: Graph builder: EventLog -> GraphModel
description:
Implement `buildGraph(log, { expanded })` in packages/log/src/graph.ts exactly as CONTRACTS.md section 8 and SPEC 'Graph construction', 'Loops and repeated calls'.

Table-driven tests from small hand-written logs (one per rule):
- function event -> call node with in-ports (type + param), const ports written as `param = text`, label inputs on the port, out-ports with bound names
- constructor -> instance node with params; method events on it -> call nodes parented to the instance, one per call site (scaler.transform on train and test = two boxes); owner not a port
- make_pipeline-style function returning a machine -> function node + instance node with createdBy
- data method (df.dropna()) -> call node with a `self` port
- machine passed as an argument -> edge from instance border
- returns_self -> no out-port; mutates on data -> changedInPlace out-port; mutates on owner -> instance versions
- expr nodes dashed, dropped when they reach no machine (transitively)
- store nodes; source nodes for tokens with no producer (and for version bumps with no event)
- same merge_key -> one node with executions sorted, slot execution included, count from the latest
- name labels: bound name in scope 0; X = X.drop(...) gives `X′` on the superseded wire
- interrupted and error executions carry through
- >300 nodes -> truncated by order with tooMany
- determinism and stable ids: building twice, and building from a log of the same program with one unrelated line changed, keeps ids of unchanged nodes.

title: Recorder: hooks, events, filtering, caps, streaming
description:
Implement python/machines/recorder.py exactly as CONTRACTS.md section 4, on top of transform.py and values.py. This is the heart of the project: SPEC's goals 'same behaviour as uninstrumented Python' and 'never draw a wire that isn't real dataflow' are this bead's acceptance bar.

- `__rec__`, `__bind__`, `__store__` (and pass-through `__scope__`, `__ret__`), installed in builtins with positional-only leading params, passing through when no Recorder is active.
- call filtering + fast path; kind detection incl. classmethods; signature binding with cache and arg0 fallback; data-method `self` input; inputs per origin with scalar identity guard and label-on-port values; outputs with unpack split and returns_self; mutates for owner, inputs and estimators reachable via get_params(deep=True)
- expr events (incl. hidden-call and past-cap fallback for `call` origins) recorded before their consumer; store events with forced bump
- module-scope bindings (scope 0) with per-site cap; `merge_key = "s<site>"`; count; per-site slot replacement; max_events -> status limit and recording stops while the code keeps running
- errors on innermost event, propagated on enclosing, handled flag when execution continues
- re-entry flag around all summarizing/fingerprinting/get_params; degrade-to-pass-through with diagnostics on internal errors
- streaming: batches per CONTRACTS.md section 7 ('batch' message shape, `open` stack), 100 ms flush check at hook entry, on_enter/on_exit callbacks
- `Recorder.log()` assembles the full EventLog (used by runtime.record).

Tests (python/tests/test_recorder.py) drive small inline programs through instrument + Recorder with a minimal exec helper (runtime.py is the next bead) and assert on the log. Cover at least: SPEC example (train_test_split -> 4 outputs with names), fit returns_self + mutates, chained fit().predict() owner, dropna(inplace=True) version bump, df['c']=v store, equal literals never share a token, np.bool_ results never share a token, models['rf'].fit owner identity, GridSearchCV original stays unfitted, kwargs named site/fn, super() in a class body method called from module level, student __repr__ not recorded, ufunc arg0 labels, a 30-iteration loop (20 full + slot, count 30), max_events limit, an exception inside a library call (error + re-raise identical), a deliberately broken summary (monkeypatched to raise) -> diagnostics and the program still runs.

Uses transform.instrument and values.ValueTable; extend those (with tests) only for small gaps and say so in the PR.
Performance: cache signatures and filter decisions; no per-call imports. Measure overhead on fixtures heavy.py vs plain and report it in the PR.
Out of scope: stdout capture, warnings, input(), tracebacks, compile/linecache (runtime bead); scopes (M4).

title: Transformer: Instrument rewrite and site table
description:
Implement `instrument(source) -> Instrumented` in python/machines/transform.py exactly as CONTRACTS.md section 3 (the M1-3 rules: module and class bodies only, function and lambda bodies untouched).

Rules that must each have a test (assert on `ast.unparse` of the result and on the site dicts):
- every Call outside function bodies becomes `__rec__(site, func, ...)`, nested calls wrapped first, arg order preserved, `*a`/`**k` preserved, origins after a starred arg are `unknown`
- bare-name calls to super/locals/globals/vars/dir/eval/exec/breakpoint are not wrapped (their arguments are)
- decorators are visited; def/async def/lambda bodies are not; generator functions untouched
- Assign/AugAssign/AnnAssign/for/with targets at module level produce `__bind__` with flattened Name targets; subscript/attribute targets with a Name root produce `__store__(site, root)`; class-body statements get neither
- origins: const (including -1 and all-const tuple/list/dict literals), name, call (with inner site id), expr with `reads` (names only, not lambda params or comprehension targets)
- `unpack` set for `a, b, c, d = f(...)` and not for `a, *b = f(...)` or nested targets
- site positions are code-point columns (test with a non-ASCII string literal before the call) and `text` is the exact source slice
- SyntaxError is raised unchanged
- the rewritten tree compiles and, with pass-through hooks installed in builtins, every fixture program produces the same stdout as the original (a cheap transparency check that doesn't need the recorder).
